    (fun a a_1 a_ih => ⟨F_1 (Lean.MessageData.withNamingContext a a_1) a_ih, a_ih⟩)
    (fun a a_1 a_ih => ⟨F_1 (Lean.MessageData.nest a a_1) a_ih, a_ih⟩)
    (fun a a_ih => ⟨F_1 a.group a_ih, a_ih⟩)
    (fun a a_1 a_ih a_ih_1 => ⟨F_1 (a.compose a_1) ⟨a_ih, a_ih_1⟩, a_ih, a_ih_1⟩)
    (fun a a_1 a_ih => ⟨F_1 (Lean.MessageData.tagged a a_1) a_ih, a_ih⟩)
    (fun data msg children msg_ih children_ih =>

    (fun f hasSyntheticSorry =>
      ⟨F_1 (Lean.MessageData.ofLazy f hasSyntheticSorry) PUnit.unit, PUnit.unit⟩)

    (fun toList toList_ih => ⟨F_2 { toList := toList } toList_ih, toList_ih⟩)
    ⟨F_3 [] PUnit.unit, PUnit.unit⟩

doc:
Creates a string describing an error message `msg` produced at `pos`, optionally ending at `endPos`,
in `fileName`.

Additional optional arguments can be used to prepend a label `kind` describing the severity of
the error (e.g., `"warning"` or `"error"`) and a bracketed `name` label displaying the name of the
error if it has one.

value.text:
fun fileName pos msg endPos kind name =>
  have endPos :=
    match endPos with
    | some endPos => toString "-" ++ toString endPos.line ++ toString ":" ++ toString endPos.column
    | none => "";
  have label :=
    if (name.isSome || kind.isSome) = true then
      have name := Option.map (fun x => toString "(" ++ toString x ++ toString ")") name;
      toString " " ++ toString (kind.getD "") ++ toString (name.getD "") ++ toString ":"
    else "";
  toString fileName ++ toString ":" ++ toString pos.line ++ toString ":" ++ toString pos.column ++
            toString endPos ++
          toString ":" ++
        toString label ++
      toString " " ++
    toString msg

doc:
Set `SourceInfo.leading` according to the trailing stop of the preceding token.
The result is a round-tripping syntax tree IF, in the input syntax tree,
* all leading stops, atom contents, and trailing starts are correct
* trailing stops are between the trailing start and the next leading stop.

Remark: after parsing, all `SourceInfo.leading` fields are empty.
The `Syntax` argument is the output produced by the parser for `source`.
This function "fixes" the `source.leading` field.

Additionally, we try to choose "nicer" splits between leading and trailing stops
according to some heuristics so that e.g. comments are associated to the (intuitively)
correct token.

Note that the `SourceInfo.trailing` fields must be correct.
The implementation of this Function relies on this property.

doc:
Rewrites links from the internal Lean manual syntax to the correct URL. This rewriting is an
overapproximation: any parentheses containing the internal syntax of a Lean manual URL is rewritten.

The internal syntax is the URL scheme `lean-manual` followed by the path `/KIND/MORE...`, where
`KIND` is a kind of content being linked to. Presently, the only valid kind is `section`, and it
requires that the remainder of the path consists of one element, which is a section or part identifier.

The correct URL is based on a manual root URL, which is determined by the `LEAN_MANUAL_ROOT`
environment variable. If this environment variable is not set, a manual root provided when Lean was
built is used (typically this is the version corresponding to the current release). If no such root
is available, the latest version of the manual is used.

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadEnv m] [Lean.MonadError m] msg declHint =>
  have msg := msg;
  do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.MessageData → m Lean.MessageData := fun __r msg => pure msg
  if
        (!declHint.isAnonymous && env.isExporting && (env.setExporting false).contains declHint) =
          true then
      have c :=
        Lean.MessageData.withContext
          { env := env.setExporting false, mctx := { }, lctx := { }, opts := ∅ }
          (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declHint);
      have msg :=
        match env.getModuleIdxFor? declHint with
        | none =>
          msg ++
            (Lean.toMessageData "A private declaration `" ++ Lean.toMessageData c ++
                Lean.toMessageData
                  "` (from the current module) exists but would need to be public to access here.").note
        | some idx =>
          have mod := env.header.moduleNames[idx]!;
          if Lean.isPrivateName declHint = true then
            msg ++
              (Lean.toMessageData "A private declaration `" ++ Lean.toMessageData c ++
                      Lean.toMessageData "` (from `" ++
                    Lean.toMessageData mod ++
                  Lean.toMessageData "`) exists but would need to be public to access here.").note
          else
            msg ++
              (Lean.toMessageData "A public declaration `" ++ Lean.toMessageData c ++
                      Lean.toMessageData
                        "` exists but is imported privately; consider adding `public import " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData mod ++
                  Lean.toMessageData "`.").note;
      __do_jp () msg
    else __do_jp () msg

doc:
Given a name `n`, return a list of possible interpretations.
Each interpretation is a pair `(declName, fieldList)`, where `declName`
is the name of a declaration in the current environment, and `fieldList` are
(potential) field names.
The pair is needed because in Lean `.` may be part of a qualified name or
a field (aka dot-notation).
As an example, consider the following definitions
```
def Boo.x   := 1
def Foo.x   := 2
def Foo.x.y := 3
```
After `open Foo`, we have
- `resolveGlobalName x`     => `[(Foo.x, [])]`
- `resolveGlobalName x.y`   => `[(Foo.x.y, [])]`
- `resolveGlobalName x.z.w` => `[(Foo.x, [z, w])]`

After `open Foo open Boo`, we have
- `resolveGlobalName x`     => `[(Foo.x, []), (Boo.x, [])]`
- `resolveGlobalName x.y`   => `[(Foo.x.y, [])]`
- `resolveGlobalName x.z.w` => `[(Foo.x, [z, w]), (Boo.x, [z, w])]`

If `enableLog` is false, this function does not ever log warnings etc, which is useful if it may be
called incidentally or multiple times.

  [Lean.MonadOptions m] [Lean.MonadLog m] [Lean.AddMessageContext m] (id : Lean.Name)
  (enableLog : Bool := true) : m (List (Lean.Name × List String))

  do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
  let __do_lift_1 ← Lean.getOptions
  let __do_lift_2 ← Lean.getCurrNamespace
  let __do_lift_3 ← Lean.getOpenDecls
  have res : List (Lean.Name × List String) :=
    Lean.ResolveName.resolveGlobalName __do_lift __do_lift_1 __do_lift_2 __do_lift_3 id
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
  have __do_jp : Unit → m (List (Lean.Name × List String)) := fun __r => pure res
  if (enableLog && __do_lift.isExporting) = true then
      match List.find? (fun x => Lean.isPrivateName x.1) res with
      | some prv => do
        let __r ← Lean.checkPrivateInPublic prv.1
        __do_jp __r
      | x => __do_jp ()
    else __do_jp ()

doc:
Finds an efficient name that unambiguously resolves to the given name `n₀`, if possible.
Considers suffixes of `n₀` and suffixes of aliases of `n₀` when "unresolving".
Aliases are considered first.

When `fullNames` is true, returns either `n₀` or `_root_.n₀`.

When `allowHorizAliases` is false, then "horizontal aliases" (ones that are not put into a parent namespace) are filtered out.
The assumption is that non-horizontal aliases are "API exports" (i.e., intentional exports that should be considered to be the new canonical name).
"Non-API exports" arise from (1) using `export` to add names to a namespace for dot notation or (2) projects that want names to be conveniently and permanently accessible in their own namespaces.

`filter` specifies a predicate that the unresolved name must additionally satisfy.

This function is meant to be used for pretty printing.
If `n₀` is an accessible name, then the result will be an accessible name.

The name `n₀` may be private.

def Lean.unresolveNameGlobal? {m : Type → Type} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadResolveName m] [Lean.MonadEnv m]
  [Lean.MonadOptions m] [Lean.MonadLog m] [Lean.AddMessageContext m] (n₀ : Lean.Name)
  (fullNames allowHorizAliases : Bool := false)
  (filter : Lean.Name → m Bool := fun x => pure true) : m (Option Lean.Name)

value.text:
fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadResolveName m] [Lean.MonadEnv m] [Lean.MonadOptions m]
    [Lean.MonadLog m] [Lean.AddMessageContext m] n₀ fullNames allowHorizAliases filter =>
  (have view := Lean.extractMacroScopes n₀;
    have n₁ := Lean.privateToUserName view.name;
    if fullNames = true then
      Lean.unresolveNameGlobal?.tryResolve✝ n₀ filter (some view) n₁ <|>
        Lean.unresolveNameGlobal?.tryResolve✝ n₀ filter (some view) (Lean.rootNamespace ++ n₁)
    else do
      let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
      have aliases : Array Lean.Name := (Lean.getRevAliases __do_lift n₀).toArray
      have __do_jp : Unit → Array Lean.Name → OptionT m Lean.Name := fun __r aliases =>
        Array.firstM (Lean.unresolveNameGlobal?.unresolveNameCore✝ n₀ filter none) aliases <|>
          Lean.unresolveNameGlobal?.unresolveNameCore✝ n₀ filter (some view)
            (Lean.rootNamespace ++ n₁)
      if allowHorizAliases = true then __do_jp () aliases
        else
          have aliases := Array.filter (fun n => n.getPrefix.isPrefixOf n₁.getPrefix) aliases;
          __do_jp () aliases).run

    [Lean.MonadLog m] [Lean.AddMessageContext m] [Lean.MonadLCtx m] n =>
  do
  let lctx ← Lean.getLCtx
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getLCtx
  have auxDeclToFullName : Lean.FVarIdMap Lean.Name := __do_lift.auxDeclToFullName
  let currNamespace ← Lean.getCurrNamespace
  have view : Lean.MacroScopesView := Lean.extractMacroScopes n
  have matchLocalDecl? : Lean.LocalDecl → Lean.Name → Option Lean.LocalDecl :=
    fun localDecl givenName => do
    guard ((localDecl.userName == givenName) = true)
    pure localDecl
  have matchAuxRecDecl? :
    Lean.LocalDecl → Lean.Name → Lean.MacroScopesView → Option Lean.LocalDecl :=
    fun localDecl fullDeclName givenNameView =>
    have fullDeclView := Lean.extractMacroScopes fullDeclName;
    have fullDeclView :=
      { name := (Lean.privateToUserName? fullDeclView.name).getD fullDeclView.name,
        imported := fullDeclView.imported, ctx := fullDeclView.ctx, scopes := fullDeclView.scopes };
    have fullDeclName := fullDeclView.review;
    have localDeclNameView := Lean.extractMacroScopes localDecl.userName;
    if currNamespace.isPrefixOf fullDeclName = true then do
      guard (localDeclNameView.isSuffixOf givenNameView = true)
      guard (givenNameView.isSuffixOf fullDeclView = true)
      pure localDecl
    else Lean.resolveLocalName.go✝ localDecl givenNameView fullDeclName currNamespace
  have findLocalDecl? : Lean.MacroScopesView → Bool → Option Lean.LocalDecl :=
    fun givenNameView skipAuxDecl =>
    have givenName := givenNameView.review;
    have localDecl? :=
      lctx.decls.findSomeRev? fun localDecl? => do
        let localDecl ← localDecl?
        if localDecl.isAuxDecl = true then do
            guard ((!skipAuxDecl) = true)
            match Std.TreeMap.get? auxDeclToFullName localDecl.fvarId with
              | some fullDeclName => matchAuxRecDecl? localDecl fullDeclName givenNameView
              | x => matchLocalDecl? localDecl givenName
          else matchLocalDecl? localDecl givenName;
    if (localDecl?.isSome || skipAuxDecl) = true then localDecl?
    else
      lctx.decls.findSomeRev? fun localDecl? => do
        let localDecl ← localDecl?
        guard (localDecl.isAuxDecl = true)
        matchLocalDecl? localDecl givenName
  Lean.resolveLocalName.loop✝ view findLocalDecl? view.name [] false

    [Lean.MonadLog m] [Lean.AddMessageContext m] n₀ filter view? n =>
  do
  guard ((!n.hasMacroScopes) = true)
  have n : Lean.Name := Lean.privateToUserName n
  have revComponents : List Lean.Name := n.componentsRev
  have candidate : Lean.Name := Lean.Name.anonymous

    forIn revComponents (none, candidate) fun cmpt __s =>
        have candidate := __s.2;

              (do
                let __do_lift ← Lean.unresolveNameGlobal?.tryResolve✝ n₀ filter view? candidate
                EarlyReturnT.return __do_lift)
              fun x => ExceptT.run (pure ())
        EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure (ForInStep.done (some r, candidate))) fun __r =>
            pure (ForInStep.yield (none, candidate))

doc:
Given a name `id` try to find namespaces it may refer to. The resolution procedure works as follows

1- If `id` is in the scope of `namespace` commands the namespace `s_1. ... . s_n`,
then we include `s_1 . ... . s_i ++ n` in the result if it is the name of an existing namespace.
We search "backwards", and include at most one of the in the list of resulting namespaces.

2- If `id` is the exact name of an existing namespace, then include `id`

3- Finally, for each command `open N`, include in the result `N ++ n` if it is the name of an existing namespace.
We only consider simple `open` commands.

doc:
A snippet of a Verso module text.

A snippet consists of text followed by subsections. Because the sequence of snippets that occur in a
source file are conceptually a single document, they have a consistent header nesting structure.
This means that initial textual content of a snippet is a continuation of the text at the end of the
prior snippet.

The actual hierarchical structure of the document is reconstructed from the sequence of snippets.

The _terminal nesting_ of a sequence of snippets is 0 if there are no sections in the sequence.
Otherwise, it is one greater than the nesting of the last snippet's last section. The module
docstring elaborator maintains the invariant that each snippet's first section's level is at most
the terminal nesting of the preceding snippets, and that the level of each section within a snippet
is at most one greater than the preceding section's level.

    if

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadError m] stx =>
  match stx.raw[1] with
  | Lean.Syntax.atom info val =>
    pure (String.Pos.Raw.extract val 0 (val.rawEndPos.unoffsetBy { byteIdx := 2 }))
  | Lean.Syntax.node info `Lean.Parser.Command.versoCommentBody args =>
    match stx.raw[1][0] with
    | Lean.Syntax.atom info val =>
      pure (String.Pos.Raw.extract val 0 (val.rawEndPos.unoffsetBy { byteIdx := 2 }))
    | x =>
      Lean.throwErrorAt stx.raw
        (Lean.toMessageData "unexpected doc string" ++
          Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofSyntax stx.raw)))
  | x =>
    Lean.throwErrorAt stx.raw
      (Lean.toMessageData "unexpected doc string" ++
        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentD (Lean.MessageData.ofSyntax stx.raw)))

Returns the character at position `p` of the input string. Returns `(default : Char)`, which is
`'A'`, if `p` is not a valid position.

Requires evidence, `h`, that `p` is within bounds instead of performing a run-time bounds check as
in `InputContext.get`.

A typical pattern combines `get'` with a dependent `if`-expression to avoid the overhead of an
additional bounds check. For example:
```
def getInBounds? (s : String) (p : String.Pos) : Option Char :=
  if h : s.atEnd p then none else some (s.get' p h)
```
Even with evidence of `¬ s.atEnd p`, `p` may be invalid if a byte index points into the middle of a
multi-byte UTF-8 character.

                errorMsg := s.errorMsg, recoveredErrors := s.recoveredErrors };

Similar to `withTraceNode`, but msg is constructed **before** executing `k`.
This is important when debugging methods such as `isDefEq`, and we want to generate the message
before `k` updates the metavariable assignment. The class `ExceptToTraceResult` is used to convert

`TraceData.result?`. The rendering layer uses `TraceResult.toEmoji` to prepend the appropriate
emoji (✅️/❌️/💥️) when displaying the trace.

doc:
Run the provided action `k`, and log its execution within a trace node.

The message is produced after the action completes, and has access to its return value.
If it is more convenient to produce the message as part of the computation,
then `Lean.withTraceNode'` can be used instead.
If profiling is enabled, this will also log the runtime of `k`.

The class `ExceptToTraceResult` is used to convert the result produced by `k` into a `TraceResult`
(success/failure/error), which is stored in `TraceData.result?`. The rendering layer uses
`TraceResult.toEmoji` to prepend the appropriate emoji (✅️/❌️/💥️) when displaying the trace.
A typical invocation might be:
```lean4
withTraceNode `isPosTrace
    (msg := fun _ => return m!"checking positivity") do
  return 0 < x
```

The `cls`, `collapsed`, and `tag` arguments are forwarded to the constructor of `TraceData`.

doc:
Pair of (optional) old snapshot task usable for incremental reuse and new snapshot promise for
incremental reporting. Inside the elaborator, we build snapshots by carrying such bundles and then
checking if we can reuse `old?` if set or else redoing the corresponding elaboration step. In either
case, we derive new bundles for nested snapshots, if any, and finally `resolve` `new` to the result.

Note that failing to `resolve` a created promise will block the language server indefinitely!
We use `withAlwaysResolvedPromise`/`withAlwaysResolvedPromises` to ensure this doesn't happen.

In the future, the 1-element history `old?` may be replaced with a global cache indexed by strong
hashes but the promise will still need to be passed through the elaborator.

doc:
Reports messages on stdout and returns the new total number of errors reported.
If `json` is true, prints messages as JSON (one per line).
If a message's kind is in `severityOverrides`, it will be reported with
the specified severity.

signature.text:
def Lean.Language.reportMessages✝ (msgLog : Lean.MessageLog) (opts : Lean.Options) (json : Bool)
  (severityOverrides : Lean.NameMap Lean.MessageSeverity) (numErrors : ℕ) : IO ℕ

value.text:
fun msgLog opts json severityOverrides numErrors =>
  have includeEndPos := Lean.Option.get opts Lean.Language.printMessageEndPos;
  msgLog.unreported.foldlM
    (fun numErrors msg =>
      have msg :=
        match severityOverrides.find? msg.kind with
        | some severity =>
          { fileName := msg.fileName, pos := msg.pos, endPos := msg.endPos,
            keepFullRange := msg.keepFullRange, severity := severity, isSilent := msg.isSilent,
            caption := msg.caption, data := msg.data }
        | x => msg;
      have numErrors :=
        numErrors +
          if
              (match msg.severity with
                | Lean.MessageSeverity.error => true
                | x => false) =
                true then
            1
          else 0;
      have maxErrorsReached :=
        Lean.Option.get opts Lean.Language.maxErrors != 0 &&
          decide (numErrors > Lean.Option.get opts Lean.Language.maxErrors);
      have msg :=
        if maxErrorsReached = true then
          { fileName := msg.fileName, pos := msg.pos, endPos := msg.endPos,
            keepFullRange := msg.keepFullRange, isSilent := msg.isSilent, caption := msg.caption,
            data :=
              (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                (toString "maximum number of errors (" ++
                    toString (Lean.Option.get opts Lean.Language.maxErrors) ++
                  toString "; from option `maxErrors`) reached, exiting") }
        else msg;
      have __do_jp := fun __r =>
        have __do_jp := fun __r => pure numErrors;
        if maxErrorsReached = true then do
          let __r ← IO.Process.exit 1
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ();
      if msg.isSilent = true then __do_jp ()
      else
        if json = true then do
          let j ← liftM msg.toJson
          let __r ← IO.println j.compress
          __do_jp __r
        else do
          let s ← liftM (msg.toString includeEndPos)
          let __r ← IO.print s
          __do_jp __r)
    numErrors

Wraps the given action for use in `BaseIO.asTask` etc., discarding its final state except for
`logSnapshotTask` tasks, which are reported as part of the returned tree. The given cancellation
token, if any, should be stored in a `SnapshotTask` for the server to trigger it when the result is
no longer needed.

fun {α} act cancelTk? desc => do
  let f ←
    Lean.Core.wrapAsync
        (fun a => do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
          IO.FS.withIsolatedStreams
              (do
                let tid ← liftM IO.getTID
                modify fun st =>
                    { env := st.env, nextMacroScope := st.nextMacroScope, ngen := st.ngen,
                      auxDeclNGen := st.auxDeclNGen, traceState := { tid := tid },
                      cache := st.cache, messages := st.messages.markAllReported }
                tryFinally
                    (tryCatch
                      (Lean.withTraceNode `Elab.async
                        (fun x => pure ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) desc)) (act a))
                      fun e =>
                      if e.isInterrupt = true then pure () else Lean.logError e.toMessageData)
                    Lean.addTraceAsMessages
                get)
              (Lean.Option.get __do_lift Lean.Core.stderrAsMessages))
        cancelTk?
  let ctx ← readThe Lean.Core.Context
  pure fun a => do
      let __do_lift ← (f a).toBaseIO
      match __do_lift with
        | Except.ok (output, st) => do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.Core.mkSnapshot? output ctx st desc
          pure (__do_lift.getD (Lean.Language.toSnapshotTree default))

doc:
Incremental reuse primitive: if `reusableResult?` is `none`, runs `act` and returns its result
together with the saved monadic state after `act` including the heartbeats used by it. If
`reusableResult?` on the other hand is `some (a, state)`, restores full `state` including heartbeats
used and returns `(a, state)`.

The intention is for steps that support incremental reuse to initially pass `none` as
`reusableResult?` and store the result and state in a snapshot. In a further run, if reuse is
possible, `reusableResult?` should be set to the previous result and state, ensuring that the state
after running `withRestoreOrSaveFull` is identical in both runs. Note however that necessarily this
is only an approximation in the case of heartbeats as heartbeats used by `withRestoreOrSaveFull`
itself after calling `act` as well as by reuse-handling code such as the one supplying
`reusableResult?` are not accounted for.

fun {α} reusableResult? act =>
  match reusableResult? with
  | some (val, state) => do
    set state.toState
    liftM (IO.addHeartbeats state.passedHeartbeats)
    pure (val, state)
  | x => do
    let startHeartbeats ← liftM IO.getNumHeartbeats
    let a ← act
    let s ← get
    let stopHeartbeats ← liftM IO.getNumHeartbeats
    pure (a, { toState := s, passedHeartbeats := stopHeartbeats - startHeartbeats })

doc:
This ref exists to break a linking cycle that goes as follows:
- We start in `Environment.lean`, there we have functions referencing the compiler such as
  `evalConst`
- This pulls in the entire compiler transitively as well as all of its dependents
- The compiler relies on things like WHNF to inspect types
- WHNF in turn imports Environment

On Windows this causes a large amount of symbols to be included in one DLL as everything that
imports the Environment instantly requires a large chunk of the Meta stack to be linked. This ref
breaks the cycle by making `compileDeclsImpl` a "dynamic" call through the ref that is not visible
to the linker. In the compiler there is a matching `builtin_initialize` to set this ref to the
actual implementation of compileDeclsRef.

fun {m} [Monad m] [Lean.MonadEnv m] [Lean.MonadError m] decl => do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  decl.forExprM fun e =>
      have unsupportedRecursor? :=
        Lean.Expr.find?
          (fun x =>
            match x with
            | Lean.Expr.const declName us =>
              (Lean.isAuxRecursor env declName && !Lean.isCasesOnRecursor env declName ||
                  Lean.isRecCore env declName) &&
                !Lean.supportedRecursors✝.contains declName

      | some (Lean.Expr.const declName us) =>
        Lean.throwError
          (Lean.toMessageData "code generator does not support recursor `" ++
              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
            Lean.toMessageData "` yet, consider using `match ... with` and/or structural recursion")
      | x => pure ()

fun name descr validate ref applicationTime asyncMode => do
  let ext ←
    Lean.registerPersistentEnvExtension
        { name := ref, mkInitial := pure ∅, addImportedFn := fun x x_1 => pure ∅,
          addEntryFn := fun s n => s.insert n,
          exportEntriesFnEx := fun env es =>
            have all := (Std.TreeSet.foldl (fun a e => a.push e) #[] es).qsort Lean.Name.quickLt;
            have exported := Array.filter (fun n => (env.setExporting true).contains n false) all;
            { exported := exported, server := exported, «private» := all },
          statsFn := fun s =>
            Std.Format.text "tag attribute" ++ Std.Format.line ++
                Std.Format.text "number of local entries: " ++
              Std.format (Std.TreeSet.size s),
          asyncMode := asyncMode,
          replay? :=
            some fun x newState newConsts s =>
              List.foldl (fun s c => if newState.contains c = true then s.insert c else s) s
                newConsts }
  have attrImpl : Lean.AttributeImpl :=
    { ref := ref, name := name, descr := descr, applicationTime := applicationTime,
      add := fun decl stx kind => do
        Lean.Attribute.Builtin.ensureNoArgs stx
        have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.AttrM Unit := fun __r => do
          let env ← Lean.getEnv
          have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.AttrM Unit := fun __r =>
            have __do_jp := fun __r => do
              validate decl
              Lean.modifyEnv fun env => ext.addEntry env decl ext.toEnvExtension.asyncMode decl;
            if ext.toEnvExtension.asyncMayModify env decl = true then __do_jp ()
            else do
              let __r ← Lean.throwAttrNotInAsyncCtx name decl env.asyncPrefix?
              __do_jp __r
          if (env.getModuleIdxFor? decl).isNone = true then __do_jp ()
            else do
              let __r ← Lean.throwAttrDeclInImportedModule name decl
              __do_jp __r
        if (kind == Lean.AttributeKind.global) = true then __do_jp ()
          else do
            let __r ← Lean.throwAttrMustBeGlobal name kind
            __do_jp __r }

  pure { attr := attrImpl, ext := ext }

          addEntryFn := fun x p =>
            match x with
            | (decls, m) => (p.1 :: decls, m.insert p.1 p.2),
          exportEntriesFnEx := fun env x =>
            match x with
            | (decls, m) =>
              Id.run
                (have all :=
                  if impl.preserveOrder = true then
                    Array.filterMap
                      (fun n => do
                        let __do_lift ← m.find? n
                        pure (n, __do_lift))
                      decls.toArray.reverse
                  else
                    have r := Std.TreeMap.foldl (fun a n p => a.push (n, p)) #[] m;
                    r.qsort fun a b => a.1.quickLt b.1;
                have exported :=
                  Array.filter
                    (fun x =>
                      match x with
                      | (n, a) => impl.filterExport env n a)
                    all;
                { exported := exported, server := exported, «private» := all }),
          statsFn := fun x =>
            match x with
            | (fst, m) =>
              Std.Format.text "parametric attribute" ++ Std.Format.line ++
                  Std.Format.text "number of local entries: " ++
                Std.format (Std.TreeMap.size m) }

    have __src := impl.toAttributeImplCore;
    { toAttributeImplCore := __src,
      add := fun decl stx kind =>
        have __do_jp := fun __r => do
          let env ← Lean.getEnv

          if (env.getModuleIdxFor? decl).isNone = true then __do_jp ()
            else do

              __do_jp __r;

        else do
          let __r ← Lean.throwAttrMustBeGlobal impl.name kind
          __do_jp __r,
      erase := fun decl =>
        Lean.throwError
          (Lean.toMessageData "Attribute `[" ++ Lean.toMessageData __src.name ++

doc:
Auxiliary function for collection the position class `outParams`, and
checking whether they are being correctly used.
A regular (i.e., non `outParam`) must not depend on an `outParam`.
Reason for this restriction:
When performing type class resolution, we replace arguments that
are `outParam`s with fresh metavariables. If regular parameters could
depend on `outParam`s, then we would also have to replace them with
fresh metavariables. Otherwise, the resulting expression could be type
incorrect. This transformation would be counterintuitive to users since
we would implicitly treat these regular parameters as `outParam`s.

doc:
Add a new type class with the given name to the environment.
`declName` must not be the name of an existing type class,
and it must be the name of constant in `env`.
`declName` must be a inductive datatype or axiom.
Recall that all structures are inductive datatypes.

signature.text:
def Lean.addClass (env : Lean.Environment) (clsName : Lean.Name) :
  Except Lean.MessageData Lean.Environment

value.text:
fun env clsName =>
  have __do_jp := fun __r =>
    match env.find? clsName with
    | some decl =>
      have __do_jp := fun __r => do
        let outParams ← Lean.checkOutParam✝ 0 #[] #[] decl.type
        have outLevelParams : Array ℕ :=
          Lean.computeOutLevelParams✝ decl.type outParams decl.levelParams
        pure
            (Lean.PersistentEnvExtension.addEntry Lean.classExtension env
              { name := clsName, outParams := outParams, outLevelParams := outLevelParams });
      if
          (match decl with
            | Lean.ConstantInfo.inductInfo val => true
            | Lean.ConstantInfo.axiomInfo val => true
            | x => false) =
            true then
        __do_jp ()
      else do
        let __r ←
          throw
              (Lean.toMessageData "invalid 'class', declaration '" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName clsName) ++
                Lean.toMessageData "' must be inductive datatype, structure, or constant")
        __do_jp __r
    | x =>
      throw
        (Lean.toMessageData "unknown declaration '" ++ Lean.toMessageData clsName ++
          Lean.toMessageData "'");
  if Lean.isClass env clsName = true then do
    let __r ←
      throw
          (Lean.toMessageData "class has already been declared '" ++
              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName clsName true) ++
            Lean.toMessageData "'")
    __do_jp __r
  else __do_jp ()

doc:
Compute positions of universe level parameters that only appear in output parameter types.

During type class resolution, the cache key for a query like
`HAppend.{0, 0, ?u} (BitVec 8) (BitVec 8) ?m` should be independent of the specific
metavariable IDs in output parameter positions. To achieve this, output parameter arguments
are erased from the cache key. However, universe levels that only appear in output parameter
types (e.g., `?u` corresponding to the result type's universe) must also be erased to avoid
cache misses when the same query is issued with different universe metavariable IDs.

This function identifies which universe level parameter positions are "output-only" by
collecting all level param names that appear in non-output parameter domains, then returning
the positions of any level params not in that set.

The following function is used to implement `end_local_scope` command.

By default, all states have `delimitsLocal` set to `true`, and the following code modifies only the top element of the stack.
If the top element’s `delimitsLocal` is `false`, the function instead traverses down the stack until it reaches the first state where `delimitsLocal` is `true`.
Intuitively, `delimitsLocal` of each `State` determines whether local entries are delimited. When set to false, it allows traversal through implicit scopes where local entries are not delimited.

doc:
Reducibility status for a definition. Controls when `isDefEq` and `whnf` are allowed to unfold it.
See `TransparencyMode` for the full design rationale.

- **`reducible`**: Unfolded at `TransparencyMode.reducible` or above. Reducible definitions still
  appear in user-facing terms, but are eagerly unfolded when indexing terms into discrimination
  trees (`simp`, type class resolution) and in `grind`. Think of it as `[inline]` for indexing.
  Suitable for abbreviations and definitions that should be transparent to proof automation.
- **`implicitReducible`**: Unfolded at `TransparencyMode.instances` or above. Used for type class
  instances and definitions that appear in types matched during implicit argument resolution
  (e.g., `Nat.add`, `Array.size`). These definitions cannot be eagerly reduced (instances expand
  into large terms, recursive definitions are problematic), but must be unfoldable when checking
  implicit arguments and resolving instance diamonds (e.g., `Add Nat` via direct instance vs via
  `Semiring`). The attribute `[implicit_reducible]` (or its alias `[instance_reducible]`) marks
  a definition with this status.
- **`semireducible`**: The default. Unfolded at `TransparencyMode.default` or above. Used for
  ordinary definitions. Suitable for user-written code where `isDefEq` should try hard during
  type checking, but not during speculative proof automation.
- **`irreducible`**: Only unfolded at `TransparencyMode.all`. The definition body is effectively
  hidden from `isDefEq` in normal usage.

fun declName status attrKind =>
  have suffix :=
    ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
        "Use `set_option allowUnsafeReducibility true` to override reducibility status validation").note;
  Lean.withoutExporting do
    let __do_lift ← Lean.getOptions
    if Lean.Option.get __do_lift Lean.allowUnsafeReducibility = true then pure ()
      else do
        let __do_lift ← Lean.getConstInfo declName
        have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.CoreM Unit := fun __r => do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
          have statusOld : Lean.ReducibilityStatus :=
            Lean.getReducibilityStatusCore __do_lift declName
          match attrKind with
            | Lean.AttributeKind.scoped =>
              Lean.throwError
                (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set reducibility status for `" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                    Lean.toMessageData
                      "`, the `scoped` modifier is not recommended for this kind of attribute" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData suffix)
            | Lean.AttributeKind.global => do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
              have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.CoreM Unit := fun __r =>
                match status with
                | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.reducible =>
                  if
                      (match statusOld with
                        | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.semireducible => true
                        | x => false) =
                        true then
                    pure ()
                  else
                    Lean.throwError
                      (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[reducible]`, `" ++
                                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "` is not currently `[semireducible]`, but `" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData statusOld.toAttrString ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                        Lean.toMessageData suffix)
                | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.irreducible =>
                  if
                      (match statusOld with
                        | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.semireducible => true
                        | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.implicitReducible => true
                        | x => false) =
                        true then
                    pure ()
                  else
                    Lean.throwError
                      (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[irreducible]`, `" ++
                                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                              Lean.toMessageData
                                "` is not currently `[semireducible]` nor `[implicit_reducible]`, but `" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData statusOld.toAttrString ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                        Lean.toMessageData suffix)
                | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.implicitReducible =>
                  if
                      (match statusOld with
                        | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.semireducible => true
                        | x => false) =
                        true then
                    pure ()
                  else
                    Lean.throwError
                      (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[implicit_reducible]`, `" ++
                                Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                              Lean.toMessageData "` is not currently `[semireducible]`, but `" ++
                            Lean.toMessageData statusOld.toAttrString ++
                          Lean.toMessageData "`" ++
                        Lean.toMessageData suffix)
                | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.semireducible =>
                  Lean.throwError
                    (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[semireducible]` for `" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                        Lean.toMessageData "`, declarations are `[semireducible]` by default" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData suffix)
              if
                    (match __do_lift.getModuleIdxFor? declName with
                      | some val => true
                      | x => false) =
                      true then
                  do
                  let __r ←
                    Lean.throwError
                        (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set reducibility status, `" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                            Lean.toMessageData
                              "` has not been defined in this file, consider using the `local` modifier" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData suffix)
                  __do_jp __r
                else __do_jp ()
            | Lean.AttributeKind.local =>
              match status with
              | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.reducible =>
                Lean.throwError
                  (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[local reducible]` for `" ++
                        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                      Lean.toMessageData
                        "`, recall that `[reducible]` affects the term indexing datastructures used by `simp` and type class resolution" ++
                    Lean.toMessageData suffix)
              | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.irreducible =>
                if
                    (match statusOld with
                      | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.semireducible => true
                      | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.implicitReducible => true
                      | x => false) =
                      true then
                  pure ()
                else
                  Lean.throwError
                    (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[local irreducible]`, `" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                            Lean.toMessageData "` is currently `" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData statusOld.toAttrString ++
                        Lean.toMessageData
                          "`, `[semireducible]` nor `[implicit_reducible]` expected" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData suffix)
              | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.implicitReducible =>
                if
                    (match statusOld with
                      | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.semireducible => true
                      | x => false) =
                      true then
                  pure ()
                else
                  Lean.throwError
                    (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[local implicit_reducible]`, `" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                            Lean.toMessageData "` is currently `" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData statusOld.toAttrString ++
                        Lean.toMessageData "`, `[semireducible]` expected" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData suffix)
              | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.semireducible =>
                if
                    (match statusOld with
                      | Lean.ReducibilityStatus.irreducible => true

                else

                    (Lean.toMessageData "failed to set `[local semireducible]`, `" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName declName) ++
                            Lean.toMessageData "` is currently `" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData statusOld.toAttrString ++

doc:
Changes the inlining behavior. This attribute comes in several variants:
- `@[inline]`: marks the definition to be inlined when it is appropriate.
- `@[inline_if_reduce]`: marks the definition to be inlined if an application of it after inlining
  and applying reduction isn't a `match` expression. This attribute can be used for inlining
  structurally recursive functions.
- `@[noinline]`: marks the definition to never be inlined.
- `@[always_inline]`: marks the definition to always be inlined.
- `@[macro_inline]`: marks the definition to always be inlined at the beginning of compilation.
  This makes it possible to define functions that evaluate some of their parameters lazily.
  Example:
  ```
  @[macro_inline]
  def test (x y : Nat) : Nat :=
    if x = 42 then x else y

  #eval test 42 (2^1000000000000) -- doesn't compute 2^1000000000000
  ```
  Only non-recursive functions may be marked `@[macro_inline]`.
